prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and quantum spin Hall effect, and for the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state

statement.case_for: I opened with WMAP, but having read the whole table I move to topological insulators as my preferred prize. It is the cleanest example of what I mean by clues from nature: Kane and Mele predicted a new Z2 class of matter from spin-orbit coupling in a graphene-like model, and Molenkamp's group then observed the protected edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, a prediction-to-measurement chain that was later confirmed in 2D and 3D materials by transport and ARPES. It has a broad and stable following of independent confirmation, it has reshaped condensed-matter physics, and it carries the widest opening support on the shortlist alongside optical lattice clocks (two first places, five rankings, including mine at rank 3). The discovery is what stands at the centre, and here the discovery is unambiguous.
statement.case_against: The attribution is genuinely untidy. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe proposal that Molenkamp's experiment tested, Zhang is deceased, and the 3D case (Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Hasan) is a further claimant, so a three-name list will leave visible gaps. There is also a novelty question relative to the 2016 prize on topological phases of matter: a sceptic could say the committee has already rewarded topology in condensed matter. I regard that as answerable, since the 2016 citation concerned topological phase transitions and the Hall plateau, not time-reversal-invariant band topology, but it must be argued explicitly in the committee's rationale.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks are a decisive instrument advance, with uncertainties near 1e-18, independent confirmation by many laboratories, and new access to relativistic geodesy, constants and dark-matter searches, with a clean Katori-Ye attribution.
responses.response: I take this seriously, and it is the strongest alternative to my choice. Metrology at the 1e-18 level is exactly the patient work that nature rewards, and the Katori-Ye attribution is much tidier than mine. My reservation is one of kind: much of the achievement is the engineering of known atomic physics, and Ye already shares the 2005 prize for the frequency comb, which sits in the same chain. The scientific discoveries enabled (relativistic redshift over millimetres, constants drift) are so far mostly demonstrations rather than findings. I do not rank it below topological insulators on rigour, but I place the discovery of a new class of matter above a record in precision. I would not object strongly if the committee settles here.

responses.point: The Z2 topological insulator theory plus the HgTe edge-channel observation is a clear case of original prediction followed by original experiment, confirmed over two decades and arguably overdue, with Zhang's role complicating the credit.
responses.response: I agree with your reading of the theory-experiment chain and of maturity. Where I want to press is the attribution you flag: leaving Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang out cannot be treated lightly, because the HgTe proposal is what told Molenkamp where to look. My answer is that the prize can be framed on the Z2 prediction and the first observation, with the experimental part resting on Molenkamp, and that Zhang's death removes one difficulty but not the Bernevig-Hughes one. I would like the committee to see an expert account of the priority between the Kane-Mele paper and the BHZ proposal before it commits.

responses.point: Circuit QED is the standard architecture for superconducting quantum processors, a two-decade confirmed platform whose prior-recognition question the 2025 prize has cleared, with Wallraff and Schoelkopf as experimental pillars and Blais as lead theorist.
responses.response: I respect the impact, but I disagree that it is as compelling as it sounds. Much of the weight is on technology and engineering that came after the 2004 demonstrations, and a four-name credit where you and Kroll disagree on who the third person is (Blais or Girvin) shows how unsettled the attribution is. After the 2025 prize on macroscopic tunnelling in circuits the committee should be careful not to reward the same community twice in consecutive years. It is a worthy candidate, but I would not choose it ahead of either topological insulators or clocks.

responses.point: IceCube's detection of a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux and its source associations opened a new observational window, with Halzen as the defensible principal laureate despite DUMAND and AMANDA claimants.
responses.response: I ranked this sixth myself, so I will not belittle it. A new messenger is as close to an existential result as the list offers. But a single-name prize on a collaboration of hundreds is a simplification I am wary of, and the source population is still incomplete (TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 are two sources and one galaxy). I would want the committee to be sure the credit would stand up before taking it, and I think that, today, a one-person IceCube prize is less secure than the topological case.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can justify a three-name credit that omits Bernevig and Hughes, and what priority the expert reports give the BHZ HgTe proposal.
Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize makes topological insulators look like a second reward for the same theme.

Whether the interest in optical lattice clocks, clearly the stronger consensus candidate among colleagues, should override my preference for a new-matter discovery; I have not ranked it myself and would defer to metrology expertise on its novelty relative to the 2005 prize.
WMAP remains my first opening choice scientifically, but only I supported it and the COBE (2006) and Peebles (2019) recognitions make it look like covered ground.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My co-author Thomas Van Riet and my supervisor David Gross have no evident link to any shortlisted candidate; my interest in dark energy is a scientific preference for WMAP, not a personal tie.
